name: Digital nomad transitory residence (Disposición 758/2022)
for: nationals of visa-exempt countries doing remote work for people or companies abroad
notes: Independent remote activity allowed

name: Business Innovation and Investment (Provisional) visa (subclass 188)
for: business owners, investors and entrepreneurs nominated by a state/territory or Austrade
notes: Closed to new applicants 31 Jul 2024 (Home Affairs). Included the Entrepreneur stream.

name: National Innovation visa (subclass 858)
for: people with an internationally recognised record of exceptional achievement (profession, sport, arts, academia/research)
notes: Invitation-only after an Expression of Interest; needs a nominator with a national reputation. Replaced Global Talent (Dec 2024). Founders qualify only on exceptional track record.

name: Red-White-Red Card for start-up founders
for: founders of innovative companies with a business plan and controlling influence
endorsement: AMS expert opinion; points test (50 of 85)
renewal: Red-White-Red Card plus after 2 years if requirements met

name: Golden Residency: Talented Individuals
for: holders of a talent certificate (academic, athletic, entrepreneurial, artistic, authors)
notes: No dedicated startup visa. Other Golden Residency tracks: BHD 200k property, or BHD 2,000 salary.

name: Barbados Welcome Stamp
for: location-independent remote workers for companies or clients outside Barbados
notes: Remote work for companies and individuals outside Barbados only

name: Professional card for self-employed non-EU nationals
for: non-EU self-employed people and company founders
endorsement: regional economic migration service (Flanders, Wallonia or Brussels)
duration: Wallonia: up to 5 years, first card usually 2 years
notes: Flanders requirements: https://www.vlaanderen.be/en/working-enterprise-and-investment/working/professional-card-for-foreign-entrepreneurs/requirements-for-a-professional-card

name: Digital nomad visa and residence (RN 45/2021)
for: remote workers for foreign employers
min_investment: none; US$1,500 per month or US$18,000 in the bank
notes: Not available for work for Brazilian employers

name: Residence for investment in innovation (RN 13/2017, amended by CNIg Res. 49/2024)
for: founders investing in innovation or R&D companies (incubated, in a tech park, or accelerated)
endorsement: Ministry of Justice and Public Security (CNIg rules)
notes: Investment from abroad with a 3-year business plan

name: Startup Visa (certificate for a high-tech or innovative project)
for: non-EU founders of innovative or high-tech businesses
endorsement: Ministry of Innovation and Growth certificate
min_investment: none; personal funds of at least 3 Bulgarian minimum wages
notes: Certificate leads to a D visa and long-term residence permit; apply via eNIMS

name: Start-up Visa Program
for: founders with a commitment from a designated VC, angel group or incubator
pr_path: yes, it is a PR route
notes: Paused 1 Jan 2026; final window for 2025 commitment-certificate holders closed 30 Jun 2026; IRCC plans a 'High Impact Start-up Pilot' with no launch date or criteria published

name: Visa Tech
for: founders and staff of technology companies
endorsement: InvestChile, Start-Up Chile or Undersecretariat of Economy sponsorship
notes: Sponsorship certificate from InvestChile; Start-Up Chile selection also supports a 1-year visa but this was not confirmed on an official page

name: Visitor visa - digital nomad
for: remote workers or freelancers for foreign companies, or founders of digital/IT ventures
min_investment: none; income of 3 monthly minimum wages for last 3 months
notes: Entrepreneurs submit a motivation letter; cannot work for Colombian employers

name: Stay for remote workers and service providers (Ley 10008)
for: remote workers and service providers for people or companies outside Costa Rica
min_investment: none; US$3,000 per month (US$4,000 with family)
notes: ICT official microsite; migracion.go.cr blocked during verification

name: Temporary stay of digital nomads
for: non-EU remote workers for a foreign employer or their own company not registered in Croatia
min_investment: none; €3,622.50 per month or €43,470 for 12 months
renewal: extension up to 6 months if first grant shorter; reapply after 6 months
notes: Cannot serve Croatian employers or clients

name: Cyprus Startup Visa
for: non-EU founders, individually or in teams, of high-growth startups
endorsement: Deputy Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digital Policy
notes: Scheme reportedly runs to Dec 2026 with quota of 150 (not confirmed on page); applications by email to startupvisa@dmrid.gov.cy

name: Key and Scientific Personnel Programme for startups
for: startups relocating key staff; long-term business visa for company executives
duration: employee card or Blue Card up to 2 years (business visa for executives)
notes: Fast-track programme, not a standalone founder visa

name: Start-up Denmark
for: founders of innovative growth companies, alone or in teams up to 3
renewal: extensions up to 3 years at a time
notes: Annual quota of 75 permits; funds are 2025 levels

name: Digital nomad visa (teleworking D visa)
for: remote workers living in Estonia while working for foreign employers or clients
min_investment: none; €3,960 per month means of subsistence
notes: Whether one's own foreign company qualifies not confirmed on this page

name: Startup Visa (D visa / temporary residence permit for startup)
for: founders of tech-based, innovative, scalable startups
duration: D visa up to 365 days; then temporary residence permit for business
renewal: D visa extendable 183 days; residence permit after company registration
processing: Startup Committee decides within 10 working days
notes: Funds figure from vm.ee fee table; Startup Estonia site still cites €800/month and €100 fee

name: Startup Permit
for: teams of at least two founders building a scalable, international startup
min_investment: none stated; sufficient funding and personal means
notes: Team must hold at least 60%; permit issued by Migri (migri.fi blocked during verification)

name: French Tech Visa for Founders (Talent Passport)
for: non-EU founders of startups recognised as innovative
endorsement: French Tech partner incubator/accelerator, French Tech Capital, or two ecosystem support letters; certificate from DRIEETS
notes: Prefecture sets the final length

name: Residence permit for self-employment (§21 AufenthG)
for: founders with economic interest or regional demand and secured financing
endorsement: local immigration office with chamber of commerce opinion
min_investment: no fixed amount; financing via capital or loan
pr_path: yes, settlement permit after 3 years if business succeeds
notes: Over-45s need pension provision; easier route for German graduates and EXIST-type scholarship holders; Opportunity Card is a job-search route, not a founder permit

name: Digital Nomad Visa
for: non-EU remote workers with employer or clients outside Greece
duration: up to 1 year (visa); residence permit up to 2 years
notes: MFA page points to workfromgreece.gr for details; no business activity in Greece allowed; apply at consulate

name: Investment as Entrepreneurs
for: entrepreneurs whose business makes a substantial contribution to Hong Kong
min_investment: no fixed minimum; capital must support the business
notes: Startups in government-backed programmes (StartmeupHK, Cyberport, HKSTP Incu-, HKDC) are viewed favourably. Mainland Chinese residents and nationals of Afghanistan, Cuba and North Korea are excluded.

name: Top Talent Pass Scheme
for: people earning HK$2.5M+ a year (A), or graduates of top universities (B: 3+ yrs experience; C: recent graduates, quota)
renewal: usually up to 3 years; business owners must show a healthy business
notes: Holders may set up or join a business without prior approval.

name: White Card (digital nomads)
for: remote workers or owners of a profitable foreign company managed from Hungary
notes: No gainful activity in Hungary and no share in a Hungarian company

name: Business visa (setting up a business venture)
for: foreigners setting up or running a business venture in India
notes: No dedicated startup visa. Founders drawing a salary from an Indian company can use the Employment visa (US$25,000/yr salary floor). Family on X visa. The MHA FAQ (403 to automated access) reportedly ties extensions to Rs 1 crore turnover.

name: Golden Visa (investor, company establishment)
for: individual investors who set up a company in Indonesia
notes: Investment must be made within 90 days of entry. The 10-year route also requires a US$50M-turnover foreign parent company.

name: Investor KITAS (E28B, company establishment)
for: foreign shareholders and directors of an Indonesian PT PMA company
notes: Allows business, investment and acting as director/commissioner. Read from the immigration visa catalogue page.

name: Remote Worker visa (E33G)
for: remote workers employed by a company outside Indonesia
notes: Requires an employment contract with a foreign company, so founders need a contract with their own foreign entity. Not for working in Indonesia.

name: Start-up Entrepreneur Programme (STEP)
for: innovative high-potential start-up founders
endorsement: evaluation committee of senior public servants
notes: Closed to Russian and Belarusian citizens; must work on the business full time; no appeal

name: Innovation Visa for a Foreign Technology Entrepreneur
for: foreign tech entrepreneurs and researchers doing R&D in Israel with a supporting framework
min_investment: none; must declare funding for living costs
notes: Procedure renewed in 2024. The Innovation Authority recommends and the Population and Immigration Authority grants. Applications are reviewed in order received; no grant included.

name: Italia Startup Visa
for: non-EU founders of innovative startups (DL 179/2012 art. 25)
endorsement: Comitato tecnico Italia Startup Visa (nulla osta)
notes: MIMIT programme portal (italiastartupvisa.mimit.gov.it) unreachable; suspended for Russian and Belarusian citizens since Oct 2023

name: Business Manager (Keiei-Kanri)
for: foreigners managing a business in Japan
min_investment: JPY 30M in total assets plus one full-time staff member (Tokyo summary of the rules)
notes: Stricter rules since 16 Oct 2025: at least one full-time employee and Japanese language ability (operator or staff). New declaration form required from 15 Apr 2026.

name: Digital nomad (Designated Activities)
for: remote workers from eligible countries earning JPY 10M or more a year
renewal: not extendable; may reapply 6 months after leaving
notes: Work must be for clients or companies outside Japan, so it suits founders of foreign companies only. Requires JPY 10M medical insurance. Eligible-country list in a separate PDF.

name: Startup Visa (Designated Activities No. 44, e.g. Tokyo)
for: foreigners preparing to start a business through a certified local government such as Tokyo
min_investment: none for the visa; switch to Business Manager needs JPY 30M in total assets plus one full-time staff member
renewal: two 6-month extensions with local-government confirmation; then switch to Business Manager
processing: 1-2 months for plan confirmation plus 1-3 months for the Certificate of Eligibility
notes: Monthly progress interviews with Business Concierge Tokyo; an office must be secured before entry. Other certified cities run similar schemes.

name: Temporary residence for foreign IT founders (Astana Hub / AIFC Expat Centre)
for: foreign founders of IT companies working with Astana Hub
notes: Founder registers a legal entity via egov.kz, then applies for a temporary residence permit through the Astana Hub/AIFC Expat Centre. Astana Hub also runs a DNV/DNR page with no readable details.

name: Class G work permit (specific trade, business or consultancy)
for: foreigners investing in a Kenyan business
gov_fee: KSh 20,000 processing + KSh 250,000 a year; free for EAC citizens
notes: No startup visa; Startup Bill still pending.

name: Temporary residence permit for start-up activities (innovative product creation)
for: non-EU founders creating or developing innovative products
notes: Page last updated Apr 2022; LIAA guide cites different funds and a qualifying investment or progress report

name: Startup Visa Lithuania
for: innovative non-EU founders
notes: Run by Innovation Agency Lithuania; free of charge; must set up the business within 120 days of the permit; suspended for Russian and Belarusian citizens

name: DE Rantau Nomad Pass
for: digital freelancers and remote workers, incl. founders/CEOs (non-tech list), with foreign-based income
renewal: renew once for 12 months (24 months max)
gov_fee: RM1,080 processing (dependant RM540) plus a security bond
notes: FAQ v10 (Aug 2026): freelancers may also serve Malaysian clients. Not open to Israeli citizens. Spouse may not work.

name: Malaysia Tech Entrepreneur Programme (MTEP)
for: tech founders and co-founders: new entrepreneurs (idea stage) or established (3+ years with 2 years of accounts)
duration: 1 year (new, PVP-MTE); up to 5 years (established, RP-MTE)
renewal: new: once for 1 more year, then may apply as established; established: 5 more years
processing: about 4 weeks plus 2 weeks for pass issuance
gov_fee: RM540 application; new entrepreneurs RM2,160 processing + RM360 pass
notes: New entrepreneurs must be sponsored by and based at a Malaysia Digital Hub or MRANTI. Figures from the MDEC MTEP FAQ (2024); the programme page itself gives no details.

name: Malta Startup Residence Programme
for: non-EU founders, co-founders and core staff of startups up to 7 years old
notes: Programme site behind bot check; figures from Residency Malta eligibility document v4.2 (Aug 2025) via search

name: Nomad Residence Permit
for: non-EU remote workers keeping work based outside Malta
renewal: renewable up to 3 times (4 years total)
notes: Site behind bot check; figures from Residency Malta FAQ via search; discretionary

name: Innovator Occupation Permit (Residency by Innovation)
for: R&D-driven startups and innovators
min_investment: none; R&D at least 20% of opex
gov_fee: US$1,000 on approval; US$50 application fee from 1 Dec 2025
notes: Project approved by the EDB, or registration with an MRIC-accredited incubator. Must reach MVP by year 5.

name: Occupation Permit for Self-Employed Entrepreneurs
for: self-employed professionals
renewal: renewable if turnover targets are met
pr_path: yes, 20-year PR after 5 years with MUR 3M/yr income
gov_fee: US$1,000 on approval; US$50 application fee
notes: Needs 3 letters of intent, 2 from local clients. Turnover targets differ on the same page.

name: Premium Visa
for: remote workers and retirees whose business and income are outside Mauritius
notes: Holder must not enter the local labour market. May later apply for an Occupation Permit.

name: IT Visa (Moldova IT Park)
for: executives, founders/shareholders in management roles and IT specialists of MITP resident companies
notes: Company must be a Moldova IT Park resident; reviewed by MITP since Law 144/2025

name: Temporary residence for digital nomads
for: remote workers for a foreign company or their own company not registered in Montenegro

name: Digital Nomad Visa
for: remote employees, freelancers and self-employed people working for clients outside Namibia
renewal: not renewable; reapply 12 months after expiry
notes: NIPDB supports the application; MHAISS issues the visa.

name: Residence permit for start-ups
for: innovative early-stage founders with a recognised facilitator
min_investment: none; enough funds for up to 1 year (or facilitator finances stay)
renewal: not extendable; switch to self-employed permit after 1 year
notes: RVO assesses the step-by-step plan; facilitator must certify at least 3 months of mentoring

name: Business Investor Work Visa
for: experienced business people buying and running an established NZ business
min_investment: NZ$1M in an established business (5+ years trading, 5+ FTE, 25%+ stake) plus NZ$500k living funds
renewal: one renewal of up to 2 years
pr_path: yes, after 3 years (12 months on the NZ$2M fast track)
notes: Not suited to startups. Replaced the Entrepreneur Work Visa.

name: Entrepreneur Work Visa
for: self-employed founders buying or starting a NZ business
notes: Closed to new applications (closure date not confirmed on an official page). The successor page refers only to past approvals.

name: Temporary residence permit for business activity
for: foreigners running a business in Poland
min_investment: none stated; sole traders must employ 2 workers or meet income tests
notes: Rules on which business forms foreigners may use

name: Residence visa for remote work (digital nomad)
for: remote professionals working for employers or clients outside Portugal
duration: visa valid 4 months, then residence permit from AIMA
notes: Income thresholds and fees not confirmed on page

name: StartUP Visa (residence for entrepreneur immigrants, art. 89(4))
for: founders of innovative, tech/knowledge-based companies
min_investment: none; about €5,146.80 per person in funds
notes: Programme page: https://startupportugal.com/programs/startup-visa/ ; target of €325k turnover/assets 5 years after incubation

name: Tech Visa
for: highly qualified non-EU tech workers hired by IAPMEI-certified companies
notes: Employer accreditation scheme; usable by founders only as employees of a certified company

name: Entrepreneur Residency (Jusour, Startup Qatar)
for: early-stage and scaling entrepreneurs endorsed by a Qatar business incubator
notes: Self-sponsored residency. Incubator nominates via Jusour; overseas founders receive an entrepreneur entry permit and then a QID.

name: Business Entrepreneur residence permit (G2)
for: non-EAC/CEPGL nationals trading goods and services on their own account
renewal: recurring permit up to 5 years with tax clearance
notes: Needs business registration, CV and police clearance. Separate Business Investor permit requires an RDB investment certificate.

name: Premium Residency: Entrepreneur
for: startup founders with a MISA entrepreneur licence and funding from a centre-accredited investor
min_investment: SAR 400k round, 20%+ stake (cat. 1); SAR 15M round, 10%+ stake, 10+10 jobs (cat. 2)
notes: Family includes parents and children under 25. Nominate 2 staff for Special Talent residency; Nitaqat exemption for 3 years.

name: Temporary residence for startup founders
for: foreigners who founded a Serbian company whose innovative activity is recognised by a public Science and Technology Park
renewal: extension needs Serbian hires, RSD 1,000,000 income, or Park confirmation
notes: Apply through welcometoserbia.gov.rs single portal

name: EntrePass
for: founders of venture-backed or innovative-tech companies holding at least 30% of a Singapore private limited company
min_investment: none stated; one of: S$100k VC/angel round, recognised incubator/accelerator, IP, research tie-up, or prior exit
renewal: first renewal up to 1 year, then up to 2 years if renewal criteria met
notes: Company over 12 months old is assessed on renewal criteria; MOM page updated Aug 2026.

name: Overseas Networks & Expertise (ONE) Pass
for: top talent earning at least S$30,000 a month, or with outstanding achievements
notes: Holder may start, operate and work for several companies at once; spouse can work on a Letter of Consent.

name: Business visa
for: foreigners establishing or investing in a South African business
min_investment: amount set by Gazette notice (certified by a chartered accountant)
notes: No startup visa. A Remote Work Visitor Visa (R650,796/yr, foreign employer contract) and a points-based work visa were gazetted in Oct 2024.

name: D-8-4 Technology Startup visa (OASIS)
for: degree holders who have set up a Korean company and score at least 80 OASIS points, or are KSGC top-20, or won over KRW 30M in a government startup project
notes: A company must already be established. A D-10-2 startup-preparation visa leads into D-8-4. The K-Startup Grand Challenge top 20 qualify directly.

name: Digital Nomad (Workation) visa (F-1-D)
for: remote workers for overseas companies or owners of overseas businesses
min_investment: income of 1-2x per-capita GNI, depending on age and region
renewal: extendable up to 3 years in total
notes: Made permanent 30 Jun 2026 after a 2024-26 pilot. Working for Korean employers is not allowed.

name: Startup Korea Special Visa (D-8-4(S))
for: foreign entrepreneurial talent recommended by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups
notes: Apply with a business plan via the K-Startup Portal or the Global Startup Center; a private evaluation committee assesses it, MSS issues a recommendation, and MOJ issues the visa. Announced Dec 2024.

name: International teleworker residence (digital nomad, art. 74 bis Ley 14/2013)
for: remote workers and self-employed professionals working for companies outside Spain
notes: Income must come from companies outside Spain; consulate guidance says self-employed may earn up to 20% from Spanish clients; owner of a foreign company not explicitly covered

name: Residence for entrepreneurs (Ley 14/2013 arts. 68-70, as amended by Startups Law Ley 28/2022)
for: founders of innovative activities of special economic interest to Spain
min_investment: none (no minimum investment or job creation)
notes: Handled by the Large Companies Unit (UGE); ENISA also certifies 'empresas emergentes' under Ley 28/2022

name: Residence permit to run your own business
for: founders owning at least 51% and running the business
min_investment: SEK 200,000 own funds (+SEK 100,000 spouse, SEK 50,000 per child)
pr_path: yes, after at least 2 years on this permit
notes: Loans normally not accepted; needs established customer contacts

name: Permit for self-employment
for: founders able to support themselves; non-EU permits limited to qualified people and quotas
notes: Federal page gives little non-EU detail; decided case by case by canton

name: Employment Gold Card
for: skilled professionals in qualifying fields
notes: Combines an open work permit, residence permit, visa and re-entry permit. Self-employment and APRC rules were not confirmed on the page read.

name: Entrepreneur Visa
for: foreign founders (alone or teams of up to 3) with VC/angel funding, NT$2M crowdfunding, incubator or accelerator residence, patents, awards, grants, or an innovative Taiwan firm with NT$1M invested
min_investment: none, or NT$1M invested in an innovative Taiwan company (criterion h)
renewal: extensions of up to 2 years if the company hits NT$3M revenue, NT$1M opex, or 3 Taiwanese full-time staff
notes: Reviewed by the MOEA Investment Commission. Apply through an overseas mission or MOFA. Directions last amended Dec 2019.

name: Long-Term Resident (LTR) visa: Wealthy Global Citizen
for: wealthy individuals with US$1M in assets
min_investment: US$500k in Thai bonds, property or direct investment in a Thai company
notes: Comes with a digital work permit. The Work-from-Thailand stream needs an employer with US$50M revenue, so it does not suit early founders.

name: SMART Visa S (Startup)
for: tech startup founders in targeted industries
notes: Requires an endorsed incubator/accelerator or government-agency endorsement, plus a Thai company set up within 1 year with at least 25% ownership or a board seat. Work permit exemption; SMART O covers dependants.

name: Turkiye Tech Visa
for: tech talent and founders of innovative tech startups
notes: Invitation programme run by the Ministry of Industry and Technology; eases residence for families.

name: Türkiye Tech Visa
for: tech talent and startups with innovative, technology-based business models
notes: Invitation programme with tax exemptions in technology development zones

name: Golden Visa: Entrepreneurs
for: entrepreneurs with an innovative or technical project
min_investment: none stated; project value must be documented
notes: Needs a letter from a business incubator or the relevant emirate authority. Self-sponsored. Thresholds (e.g. AED 500k project) not shown on u.ae.

name: Virtual work (remote work) residence visa
for: people employed by a company outside the UAE
notes: Self-sponsored. u.ae does not say whether owners of foreign companies qualify. Apply via ICP or GDRFA Dubai.

name: Global Talent visa (digital technology and other fields)
for: leaders or potential leaders in digital technology, research or arts
renewal: extendable 1 to 5 years at a time, no limit
pr_path: yes, after 3 or 5 years depending on route
processing: about 3 weeks outside UK, 8 weeks inside
notes: Founders commonly use the digital technology route

name: Innovator Founder visa
for: founders of new, innovative, viable, scalable businesses
renewal: extendable 3 years at a time, no limit; endorsing-body checkpoints at 12 and 24 months
processing: about 3 weeks outside UK, 8 weeks inside
notes: English requirement; £500 per endorsement check-in

name: E-2 Treaty Investor
for: treaty-country nationals investing in and directing a US business
renewal: extensions of up to 2 years, unlimited
notes: Requires at least 50% ownership or operational control

name: International Entrepreneur Parole (International Entrepreneur Rule)
for: founders of US startups formed within 5 years with high growth potential
endorsement: none; qualified US investors or government grants
min_investment: US$311,071 qualified investment or US$124,429 government grants
renewal: re-parole up to 2.5 more years (5 max)
notes: Parole, not a visa; up to 3 founders per startup; DHS proposed rescission in 2018 but no final rule seen on USCIS page

name: O-1A visa (extraordinary ability in business or sciences)
for: founders with sustained national or international acclaim
notes: Needs a US employer or agent petitioner, which can be the founder's own company

name: Digital nomad permit (Decree 238/022)
for: remote workers for foreign companies or self-employed
notes: Online application after entering as a tourist

name: IT Visa (IT Park)
for: founders of IT Park resident companies, IT investors (US$10k+), and IT specialists (US$30k income)
min_investment: none for founders; US$10,000 for investors
notes: Work without a work permit. Founder's company must be on the IT Park register. Apply via it-relocation.uz.
